title: fix(plugin-form): the default object-form arm builds sections through the shared section builder (objectui#10475)
body:
Fixes #10475

Clause-②: no

objectui#10476 is folded into this card by triage (closed there as a duplicate, same file and same mechanism); its half, the dropped section-entry overrides, is implemented here too.

## What changed

With explicit `sections` and no `formType`, `SimpleObjectForm` (the default `object-form` arm) resolved each section's members with its own name filter over its field pool. So the members came out in POOL order, and a spec `FormFieldSchema` entry kept only `visibleOn` / `colSpan` / `span`. The `drawer`, `modal`, `tabbed`, `wizard` and `split` arms build a section through `buildSectionFields` / `normalizeSectionField`, in the section's authored order and with the full override set.

- `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts`: `SectionFieldsContext` gains an optional `pool`. When it is set, `buildSectionFields` still walks the entries in AUTHORED order and applies each entry's overrides with the same code (`normalizeSectionField`'s body, now the module-private `resolveSectionEntry`). The pool decides two things. First, membership: an entry naming a field the pool does not hold is dropped, which is objectui#9884's intersection (the caller keeps its warning). Second, the BASE: a name string draws the pooled field as it is, and a spec entry's overrides are written onto a copy of the pooled field. An already-built runtime FormField entry is its own definition, as on the other arms, and the pool only gates it. `sectionEntryName` spells the entry identity rule once. With no `pool`, the code path the other five arms take is unchanged: the same `map` over `normalizeSectionField`. `buildSectionFields` now also accepts a section whose `fields` is optional (type-only; the body already read `section.fields ?? []`).
- `packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx`: the grouped branch builds each section with `applyFieldPerms(buildSectionFields(section, sectionCtx))`, where `sectionCtx.pool` is the arm's `sourceFields`. The name filter and the three-key copy are deleted. The objectui#9884 warning block is unchanged and now reads its names through `sectionEntryName`. The objectui#7051 `?? []` containment stays.
- The two member pins that recorded the pool order as behaviour, flipped in the same change: row 1 of `objectFormSectionMembers-8071` and row 1 of `masterDetailSectionMembers-8071` (the master-detail parent half renders through `SimpleObjectForm`). Each flip is noted in its header, as the earlier flips in those files are. The two `MEMBER_PINS` descriptions of those rows in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` are updated too, because their prose described the old row. The `sectionsCustomFields-10254` header sentence about the default arm copying only three keys is now past tense.
- New pin `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/sectionEntryOverrides-10475.test.tsx` covers the triage execution note 3, on all six arms through the real `ObjectForm`: ORDER (a two-member section in reverse pool order renders in the section's order), LABEL, REQUIRED (asterisk, `aria-required`, the empty submit is refused with "SECTION LABEL is required" and `create` is not called, the filled submit goes through), and VISIBLEWHEN (hidden for the opening record, drawn once the predicate turns true). Two more rows are default-arm only and cover what stays pool-driven: the pooled field is the base, so an override does not lift the managed-object lock the pool carries (control: the same section on an unmanaged object is editable); and FLS still gates every member, so a read-denied member is not drawn and a write-denied member keeps no enabled control even under an entry `readonly: false` (control: an unrestricted principal draws all three).
- `sectionFields.test.ts`: unit rows for the pool (order, intersection in all three shapes with a no-pool control, pooled base as-is, overrides on a copy with the pool untouched, `readonly: false` cannot re-open a locked pooled field, a runtime entry drawn as itself) and for `sectionEntryName`.
- `.changeset/10475-default-arm-section-builder.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch.

## PM mechanism hypotheses, measured

- H1, confirmed: the name filter over `sourceFields` (a `sectionFieldNames.includes` test, wrapped in `applyFieldPerms`) and the three-key copy were on the branch base `111fa4c`.
- H2, falsified in the "unchanged" half: `normalizeSectionField` builds its own base (`fromObjectSchema` or the `customFields` member). That base lacks the facts only the default arm's generator writes, such as the managed-object blanket lock (ADR-0092 D4), `inputType`, `step`, `widget`, the file `accept` and size hint, and object-level `visible_on`. Calling it unchanged would have unlocked managed objects in sectioned default forms. So the builder takes one parameter (`pool`), added in one place. The five arms' path is the unchanged `map`, and the ablation A2 below shows the pooled base is what the managed-lock row depends on.
- H3, confirmed: REQUIRED blocks the submit on all six arms, and the assertion goes beyond the asterisk.
- H4, confirmed: FLS gates the built members, applied after the overrides, which is the order the drawer and modal arms use. Ablation A3 below.

## Tests (final head `6931629`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/ apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` (through the shared verify lock), exit 0: `Test Files 120 passed (120)`, `Tests 1431 passed | 1 skipped (1432)`.
- `pnpm turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --concurrency=2`, exit 0: `Tasks: 13 successful, 13 total`. The echoed script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all five touched test files.
- `pnpm exec eslint --format json` on the 8 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files, exit 0: 8 files, 0 errors, 107 warnings (`no-explicit-any` and `react-hooks`, almost all on untouched lines). The narrowing is exact for the files it covers, because `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions` / `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- Exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (`VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`), `check:changeset-claims` (report-only: five pending changesets name a touched file, and each paragraph was read; none is falsified by this change), `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (1 changeset declared). Two gates were added because they read touched files: `check:installed-pin-claims` and `check:component-surface-parity`, both exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-examples`, reason `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (it needs about 30 packages built). The only `ObjectForm.tsx` JSDoc example it reads is untouched. Left to CI.

## Ablations (each on committed code, through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode; each restore proven with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- A1: the old default-arm build put back (the name filter plus the three-key copy). 8 red: exactly the 4 `formType: simple` rows ORDER / LABEL / REQUIRED / VISIBLEWHEN (the other five arms' 20 rows stay green), the 2 default-arm rows, and both flipped row-1 pins. 35 green.
- A2: the pooled base removed (spec entries start from the member / `fromObjectSchema` again). 3 red: the managed-lock row, plus the two unit rows on the pooled base. 50 green.
- A3: `applyFieldPerms` removed from the default arm's section members. 1 red: the FLS row. 52 green.

## Acceptance notes

- `{ group }` reference sections and field-group-derived sections on the default arm now draw in their resolved `fields` order, which is the declaration order, as on the other arms. When a top-level `fields` lists the same members in a different order, the section order now wins over it.
- A runtime FormField entry (shape 3) inside a section on the default arm is now drawn as its own definition when its name is pooled, as on the other arms. It used to draw the pool member plus the three keys. An entry whose `field` is the metadata object used to be dropped silently, because its lookup key was that object, and it is now drawn by `name`. A name listed twice in one section is now drawn twice, as on the other arms; the filter used to de-duplicate it. No fixture, example or doc in the tree authors either shape.
- `content/docs` and the package README state nothing about the default arm's section order or override set, so no doc text went false.
- The `object-form.sections` `MEMBER_PINS` description still carries an older sentence saying a `collapsed`-but-not-`collapsible` section renders permanently closed. objectui#9780 made that stale, not this change, so it is left alone.

## Out of scope, measured by a scratch probe (not committed), handed to the seat

The probe is `probe-fls-arms`: real `ObjectForm`, one section `['customer', 'amount']`, create mode, each of the six arms, run on `6931629`.

- FLS: with `MePermissionsProvider` denying `invoice.amount` read, `simple`, `drawer` and `modal` draw `['customer']`, while `tabbed`, `wizard` and `split` draw `['customer', 'amount']`. The three arms never call `applyFieldPermissions` at render.
- Managed-object lock: for a `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object with no `userActions.create`, the default arm draws 0 enabled inputs, while each of the other five draws 2. Only `ObjectForm.tsx` calls `resolveEffectiveCrudAffordances`.
